profile.reading: This registry row, Involta Independence, is named for its own Independence, Ohio facility name and sits at 7300 East Pleasant Valley Road, Independence, Ohio, in Cuyahoga County, part of the Cleveland metro. The operator's public site, still resolving at the involta.com domain but branded Ark Data Centers throughout, including in its own copyright footer, confirms this is a genuine company rebrand rather than a sale to an unrelated third party. This registry records the current name as Ark Data Centers with Involta retained as former operator per its standard no-deletion policy. Ark's own Ohio operations page describes this Independence, or Cleveland area, location as providing 2.5 megawatts of power capacity and 10,000 square feet of conditioned data center space, with 2N UPS battery backup and N+1 computer room air conditioning, and states the Akron and Cleveland facilities are linked by a dedicated fiber ring offering millisecond latency between sites, including this registry's separate Involta-Akron row roughly 30 miles away. Ark's own about page states the company was founded in 2007 as a Tier III edge data center provider and now operates purpose built, owned and operated facilities across eight markets including Arizona, Idaho, Iowa, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. Company wide certifications listed on Ark's own site include HITRUST CSF, PCI, NIST, HIPAA, ITAR, and ITIL. This row's street address was not independently corroborated by a dedicated aggregator listing this session, resting instead on a third party reverse geocode of this row's own coordinates that matched the facility's own Independence name, a lower confidence source than the operator specific aggregator match applied to the Akron row, and is recorded here with that caveat. Cuyahoga County, Ohio, home to Cleveland and this Independence facility, is a Rust Belt market whose edge colocation demand tends to come from regional healthcare systems, manufacturers, and enterprises seeking a Tier III facility close to home rather than a coastal or hyperscale cloud availability zone, a positioning consistent with Ark's own self description as a Tier III edge data center provider dating to its 2007 founding.

reading.body:
Ohio's data center market has 76 mapped facilities, but only eight publish power capacity figures, leaving 88 percent of sites unmeasured and their relevance to AI infrastructure unknowable.

Involta Independence, near Cleveland, holds Tier III certification and claims 100 percent power delivery availability, standards that support continuous production workloads. The operator lists it as one of ten enterprise-class facilities but discloses no megawatt capacity for this specific campus. Without that figure, the facility cannot be ranked against peers or assessed for scale.

For AI scaling, power capacity is the direct constraint on compute density. A facility may be operationally sound and geographically positioned in the industrial Midwest, but without knowing whether it delivers 5 megawatts or 50, its actual role in the infrastructure pipeline remains opaque. The absence of disclosure is itself data: it suggests either limited scale, reluctance to publish, or data not yet collected by this registry.

This entry covers what the operator has certified and where the facility sits. It does not reveal whether Involta Independence has spare power to expand, whether it is reserved for existing tenants, or how its capacity compares to the eight Ohio sites that do report figures. Those gaps are the binding constraint on understanding its value to AI.
